description: Published aquaponics observations (beyond UVI) used to validate the daily simulation. Observed values are evidence; 'derived' values are arithmetic on printed numbers. Read through fetch summaries, so check quotes against the PDFs before promotion.

records.name: Knaus, Appelbaum and Palm 2018, Rostock, tilapia unit (II), autumn herbs
records.source: Significant factors affecting the economic sustainability of closed backyard aquaponics systems. Part IV: autumn herbs and polyponics. AACL Bioflux 11(6):1760-1775

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Full measured fish and water record with N basis stated; small backyard unit; read through a fetch summary. Methods re-read from the PDF 2026-11-26 (bed construction, light method, Table 3). Basil planting, SD and the authors' pH statement re-read 2026-11-26 (validation round 3).

context.location: northern Germany glasshouse, autumn (8 Aug to 16 Oct 2014)
context.light: low, PAR about 111 to 147 umol/m2/s plus night tubes

inputs.note: Start biomass 10.33 kg does not equal 309 x 26.5 g (8.19 kg) as printed; the model uses the printed biomass.
inputs.dli_basis: derived, revised 2026-11-26: unit II (tilapia) daytime PAR 146.6 umol/m2/s (Table 3, twice-weekly readings) over the mean astronomical day length at Rostock (54.1 N) for 8 Aug to 16 Oct 2014, 12.65 h (our arithmetic); high = PAR held all day plus night PAR 11.6 umol/m2/s for the remaining 11.35 h (lamps assumed on all night); low = PAR read near midday on a sinusoidal day (daytime mean = 2/pi of the reading), no night light. The earlier 12.7 treated daytime PAR as a 24 h mean, which the separately reported night PAR (11.6) rules out; the earlier low (4.8) used unit I PAR (111.2) by mistake. Added 2026-11-26 (validation round 3): mid = midpoint of the two bounds (our arithmetic), used as the scored case because the photoperiod is not reported; the bounds become a sensitivity band.
inputs.basil_density_note: 12 basil per 2 m2 box (about 6 basil/m2), 36 herbs per box (18 plants/m2)

grow_bed.regime: ebb-and-flow, bell siphon, 2 L/min inflow per box

gravel_bulk_density_kg_m3_proxy.basis: sand bulk density from Maucieri et al. 2019 (Tier 1, via equipment research notes), used as a proxy because no gravel value was found; assumption

gravel_volume_m3_total_derived.basis: 2,000 kg / 1,600 to 1,400 kg/m3 (our arithmetic); the paper gives mass, not volume or depth

grow_bed.note: The paper prints 120 L water per box at maximum flood, not 2 m2 x 0.20 m = 400 L; the gravel displaces part of the box volume. No separate biofilter; a 1 m3 IBC clarifier only.

inputs.planting_material: seeded in rockwool cubes three weeks before the trial and planted into the boxes at the start (Methods); no cuts or harvest dates reported, so the 16.1 g is read as one mean per plant over the 70 days
inputs.basil_seed_source: Kiepenkerl (BALDUR Garten GmbH); cultivar not named
inputs.pH_note: pH 8.0 is the reported trial mean; the authors write that plant growth was 'generally below expectations (strongly influenced by a high alkaline pH)'. Validation runs hold pH at this mean.

observed.tan_basis_note: Printed as NH3-N 0.21 +/- 0.16 mg/L (global mean of fish tank, clarifier and sump); read as total ammonia N (photometric method), since 0.21 mg/L un-ionised NH3 at pH 8.0 would imply about 3.6 mg/L TAN (our arithmetic, Emerson pKa at 26.3 C). Hydroponic boxes 0.16 +/- 0.08.
observed.basil_note: Table 2, 'Basil fresh biomass [g]', unit II 16.1 +/- 13.8 (unit I, carp, 22.1 +/- 17.5; not significantly different). The SD is 86 percent of the mean.

records.name: Savidov 2005, Crop Diversification Centre South, Brooks, Alberta, tilapia + basil raft
records.source: Evaluation and development of aquaponics production and product market capabilities in Alberta, Phase II, final report 20 Dec 2005

review_metadata.source_gate_reason: Provincial research centre report, not peer reviewed, read via an Issuu re-host.
review_metadata.confidence_reason: Yield bases conflict between abstract and body; harvest weight per fish is derived; supplemental light.

observed.fish_harvest_basis: 378.0 kg average harvest per tank / 600 fish stocked (no mortality assumed); text also says 0.50 to 0.64 kg per fish

fish_harvest_mean_g_text_range.basis: report text: '0.50 to 0.64 kg per fish' (already recorded in fish_harvest_basis); used as the scored range from 2026-11-26 because the 630 g point assumes no mortality

records.name: Khater et al. 2023, Benha, Egypt, Nile tilapia + lettuce, hydraulic loading trial
records.source: Study on the plant and fish production in the aquaponic system as affected by different hydraulic loading rates. Scientific Reports 13:17505

review_metadata.confidence_reason: Direct table values; feed input not reported; winter greenhouse.

inputs.feed: not reported: 'daily feed rates at different fish sizes were applied according to' Rakocy 1989; fish weighed every ten days
inputs.stocking: 75 fingerlings of 40 g per 0.60 m3 tank (5 kg/m3)

observed.fcr_quality_note: Eq. 5 prints FCR = FI / (WG x nt), with WG defined as per-fish mass gained and nt the final fish count; feed intake (FI) is not printed, so the FCR cannot be recomputed. FER = 1/FCR in every row (consistent). The values (0.92 to 1.20) are below the Tier 1 range of 1.4 to 1.8 (SRAC 282, FAO 589) and below UVI's measured 1.71 to 1.92. Not scored in validation (UQ-017).

scoring_choices_approval.scope: B1-B4: validation-run setup and scoring choices (pH held at the published mean; Knaus basil scored at mid DLI; Savidov fish scored against the report's 0.50-0.64 kg range; Khater FCR reported but not scored). Condition: summaries say '0 of 10 scored, 3 reported unscored', never 'passes' or 'validated'; UQ-017 and UQ-018 stay open. The observations themselves stay candidates.
